scope: WPF combat rhythm and public card feedback

findings.before: Accepted public card, response and damage cues started together. A declared Slash also drew a large target-portrait strike before the committed outcome.

changes: Arc, tilt, short trail and landing rim for public card flights; settled card faces still align with their existing public row.
Incoming Slash, FireSlash and ThunderSlash stop at the target edge; portrait impact belongs only to committed damage.
Short, bounded visual ordering for rapid attack/result and attack/Dodge sequences; late human responses appear immediately.
Outlined floating HP amounts pop and rise without a rectangular notification box.
HitSequence and DodgeSequence preview examples use the exact live effect layer.

regressions: At 180ms, attack-only, eventual-hit and eventual-Dodge frames are identical; results have not yet appeared.
At 380ms, a declaration alone leaves the target portrait interior unchanged.
At 650ms, hit and Dodge produce distinct rendered outcomes.
A response after the declaration expires appears immediately.
Motion off, collection reset and unload cancel scheduled effects.
Native declined Slash commits revision 12 to 13 and HP 5 to 4; four player-safe snapshots and accepted commands are unchanged by rendering and retirement.
Existing public identity, converted card art, prompt protection, replay and settled-flight alignment checks pass.

renderPreparationProbe.scope: DrawingContext preparation only; not foreground FPS or input latency.

limits: No foreground physical keyboard/mouse, multi-DPI or audio acceptance.
Vector effects and static-seat reaction remain an incremental game presentation; skill staging, HP transition and audio synchronization need further iteration.
Routine remains about 125 seconds, above the approximately one-minute target.
No manual full verification, release/publish, commit or push.

cleanup.reason: Earlier exact-path removal was blocked by policy. Reused outputs registered; no automatic deletion retry.
